newsitem.title: USA: CME volume rises 12.9 pct yr/yr to record Sept.
newsitem.headline: CME volume rises 12.9 pct yr/yr to record Sept.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said volume in September rose to 19,330,620 contracts, a record for the month and up 12.9 percent from 17,115,801 traded in September 1995.
Average daily volume last month was 966,531 contracts, up from 855,790 in September 1995. Both September 1995 and September 1996 had 20 trading days.
Open interest at month's end stood at 5,801,999, up 8.8 percent from 5,330,334 at the end of September last year.
Year-to-date volume totalled 154,125,987, off 4.1 percent from 160,735,488 traded during the same nine months last year.
Since January 1994 CME has counted in volume anything that creates or liquidates open positions including expired options and SIMEX mutual offset transactions cleared on the CME.
Excluding these transactions, CME "pit traded" volume for September 1996 totaled 16,349,730 and year-to-date volume stood at 138,377,895.
